key_insight: Combining structured EHR features, clinical text embeddings, and knowledge-grounded symbolic extraction increased sensitivity for 30-day diabetic readmission prediction, but slightly reduced AUROC.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help flag more patients who will be readmitted, although its low specificity may increase false alerts.
method: Fuse engineered EHR features with 32 compressed Bio_ClinicalBERT embedding components.
Extract symbolic entities using a clinical language model with hybrid retrieval, re-ranking, and negation auditing.
Predict with cost-sensitive XGBoost and calibrate the decision threshold using Youden’s J statistic.
evidence_signal: On a patient-grouped held-out test set of 20,153 encounters, sensitivity rose from 0.5839 to 0.6667 and Brier score improved from 0.1080 to 0.0977, while AUROC fell from 0.6477 to 0.6375.
watch_item: External and prospective validation are not reported in the abstract; the separate 500-note Hinglish benchmark does not establish real-world readmission performance.
paper_title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction
